With a registration the council renews after flock inspections, a single falcon check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the lantern of that gap is the whole defence in one line. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the ledge of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
